messages:
Maya (PM): quick thread — we need to lock the next model onboarding sequence for Q2. customers asking for better summarization quality and lower latency on embeddings. options: Llama3-70B-v2, OpenLLaMA-33B-quant, and a customer-requested Claude-variant (enterprise). Thoughts on prioritization (RICE/impact vs effort) and launch criteria?
Jamal (ML Eng): quick gut: Llama3-70B-v2 = highest quality but heavy on infra. OpenLLaMA quant = low-latency cost win but risk on quality. Claude-variant = high enterprise impact but legal/contracting + infra gating.
Zoe (SRE): from SLO side: 70B will push p95 unless we do aggressive KV-cache + batching. We can meet 200ms p95 for embeddings only if we quantize and tune kernels.
David (EngInfra): infra effort estimates: Llama3-70B-v2 ~ 6 dev-weeks for serving + perf tuning on dedicated; OpenLLaMA quant ~ 3 weeks to validate quant pipeline; Claude-variant depends on licensing, estimate unknown.
Jamal (ML Eng): proposing a lightweight RICE sketch to compare — rough numbers: 
```
# model: R (reach) I (impact) C (confidence) E (effort weeks) => RICE score
Llama3-70B-v2: 8 8 0.6 6 => (8*8*0.6)/6 = 6.4
OpenLLaMA-33B-quant: 6 6 0.7 3 => (6*6*0.7)/3 = 8.4
Claude-variant (customer): 4 9 0.4 8 => (4*9*0.4)/8 = 1.8
```
Numbers are fuzzy but show OpenLLaMA quant looks like best efficiency; Llama3 wins on absolute impact.
Alex (Head Product): flag: customers asking for Llama3-quality outputs. Even if OpenLLaMA looks better RICE, if it regresses on our core benchmarks it's a bad customer experience. We should weight regression risk heavier in confidence.
Maya (PM): Agreed — let's add launch gating:
- perf: p95 latency target per route (embeddings <=200ms hosted, gen <=800ms for short prompts)
- quality: pass regression on our eval suite (no >5% drop on top-5 benchmarks)
- infra: autoscale + fallback to smaller variant on high load
- observability: token-level cost + alerts for perplexity drift
If a model can't meet these, it can't go to GA.
Zoe (SRE): also add canary rollout checklist: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% with auto-rollback on error rate >1% or latency regress >20%. ops-bot will enforce.
ops-bot: note added to rollout policy log: canary thresholds configured for product channel.
Jamal (ML Eng): operational sequencing I'd suggest: 1) OpenLLaMA-33B-quant (low effort, quick wins on cost/latency, validate quant pipeline), 2) Llama3-70B-v2 (high-impact, dedicate perf work + kernel tuning), 3) Claude-variant (only after legal + sales signoff). That lets us ship cost improvements early while investing in the big win.
Alex (Head Product): +1 to Jamal's sequence, with caveat: if OpenLLaMA fails quality checks, pivot team to Llama3. Put quality gates early in the pipeline.
Maya (PM): decision summary:
- Sequence: OpenLLaMA-33B-quant (sprint A), Llama3-70B-v2 (sprint B), Claude-variant (Q3 enterprise track)
- Launch criteria: use the gating list above (perf, quality, infra, observability, canary)
- Owners: Jamal = ML lead for quant + Llama3 tuning, Zoe = SRE lead for canary & SLOs, David = infra for dedicated config, Maya = PM to own roadmap comms, Alex = stakeholder for enterprise escalation
Action items:
- Jamal: create evaluation harness for OpenLLaMA quant by EOD Fri (1751420000)
- Zoe: draft canary runbook + alert rules by next Tue
- David: estimate dedicated capacity cost for Llama3 and share pricing with sales
- Maya: update public roadmap and announce sequence in product channel after we close evaluations
Anyone object to this plan? :thinking_face:
